title: Finite pure-tensor coordinates of the ordered negative Koszul tensors
statement: Let (C,J,O) be a small ringed site with commutative ring sheaf O [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], A a commutative ring and rho:A -> Gamma(O) a coefficient map. Let a:Fin r -> A, allowing r=0. For the actual ordered negative Koszul tensor functors T_m(K)=K tensor_O tensor_i[O --rho(a_i)^(m+1)--> O] [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], there are degreewise finite-subset coordinate isomorphisms T_m(K)^q = direct_sum_I K^(q+|I|), natural transition maps T_(m+1)->T_m and natural inclusions K->T_m satisfying the differential, coefficient-map, transition, and inclusion matrix equations of [def-cbc-signed-koszul-completion-model]. The coordinate inclusions are precisely the pure tensors ringedNegativeKoszulSummand, and the inclusions commute with the transitions. Each functor T_m preserves quasi-isomorphisms of arbitrary unbounded complexes. This finite statement involves no products, fibre, localization or coefficient-functor comparison.

proof.text: Induct on the ordered number of factors. For the empty tensor the right unitor identifies K tensor O[0] with K. For the successor split subsets by whether they contain index zero, and identify the two supported degrees of the new negative factor with O. Distribute tensor over the finite sums. Tensor unitors and total tensor inclusions give the specified pure-tensor inclusions; multiplication gives the inverse coordinates. Naturality makes maps of K diagonal. Expanding the signed total differential gives d_K plus the erased-index coefficients (-1)^(q+|I|)(-1)^#{j in I:j<i} a_i^(m+1), with precisely the equality transports in the Lean statement.

proof.text: Define transitions by conjugating the diagonal scalar product over I by these coordinates. The chain equation is (product over I of a_j) a_i^(m+1) = a_i^(m+2)(product over I.erase i of a_j). Empty-coordinate inclusions are chain maps and commute with the transitions because the empty product is one. All formulas apply at r=0 and require no scalar inversion.

proof.text: Filter each tensor by subset cardinality at most k. The kth quotient is the finite sum of copies of K reindexed by |I|=k; multiplication by the standard degreewise signs identifies these with usual shifts. A quasi-isomorphism of K induces a quasi-isomorphism on each quotient. These short exact sequences are degreewise split, so the long exact homology sequences and induction on k give quasi-isomorphism invariance of the finite total tensor, even when K is unbounded.
